product_problems: Application Program Freezes or Fails to Launch
records.text: It was reported that the EPIQ CVxi Ultrasound System froze with an error message during a TTEER (Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair). The system required multiple reboots to clear the freezing, and an exchange of the ICE Catheter was made without resolving the problem. The procedure was completed by using a TEE transducer instead of an ICE Catheter. There was no user or patient harm. Philips has started an investigation, and upon completion, a follow up report will be submitted.

One of the patient exams performed on the Juniper system displays an "Unarchived" error message and they are unable to send this study to PACS. All other exams performed before are after this one are transferring over to the PACS as expected without any errors. The problem occurred after a Breast study was completed and the user tried to send it over to the network PACS. TSE worked with the customer and she confirmed that the problem cannot be reproduced, as it only is affecting this one exam. There were no reported injuries but the entire exam was lost and they had to call the patient back in to re-do the study. The customer has not been routinely clearing out the database. The exam is corrupted and cannot be retrieved. An investigation is ongoing at Siemens Healthineers to identify the root cause of the issue. The report will be supplemented after the investigation is completed. Reference# (b)(4).

records.text: The report is being submitted as a part of a containment action for CAPA 2026-000014, which was initiated to address the FDA form 483 Observation #1 received on 27-August-2026.The complaint submitter stated that the ACUSON Origin System lis showing error message "clip aborted" and cannot save cine clips. Customer rebooted the system 3 times and which temporarily fixed issue. No patient injury or adverse outcome was reported. NOTE: Our standard procedure is to submit Medical Device Reports (MDRs) directly through our complaint handling software. Because this specific complaint record is closed, software constraints necessitate a manual submission. To maintain the integrity and continuity of the automated submission sequence for active complaints, this manual report has been assigned MDR# 3023245-2026-01002. Engineers reviewed the log files provided and stated that they do not include (b)(6) 2026 data (logs from this time is unavailable). However, the provided logs showed the error described by the customer: system displayed error message "clip aborted" and could save cine clips. Issue initially started with first clip store lag.Engineers also checked that the D drive storage space was less:-D drive:Size 894.25 GB (960,195,719,168 bytes),Free Space 390.37 GB (419,152,347,136 bytes).The root cause was determined as a software defect, where the system displays error message when customer has several hundreds of patients in the database. The issue was resolved at the site by rebuilding the database. This issue is improved in the software patch VC10 via Defect (b)(4).Reference# (b)(4).

The ACUSON Sequoia locked up during an interventional procedure with Ultrasound support for localization. An error message was displayed. The system was only recoverable for a few minutes at time. After the second lock up occurred, the system was replaced to complete the exam. No patient injury or adverse patient outcome was reported. The procedure was completed successfully using another ultrasound system, with no reported death, serious injury, or medical intervention attributable to the malfunction. An investigation is ongoing at Siemens Healthineers to identify the root cause of the issue. The report will be supplemented after the investigation is completed. Reference #(b)(4).

product_problems: Adverse Event Without Identified Device or Use Problem
records.text: On (b)(6)2026, a male patient underwent Aquablation therapy for symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). PROCEPT became aware that, post-Aquablation therapy, the patient presented with a rectal perforation. According to the information received, the night following the procedure, the patient complained of pain. A computed tomography (CT) scan was subsequently performed, which identified a rectal perforation. The patient required additional surgery to repair the perforation and currently has a temporary stoma in place as part of the postoperative management. Additional information indicated no resistance during TRUS probe insertion and no blood on the TRUS probe upon removal. According to the treating surgeon, the confirmed cause of the perforation remains unknown. No malfunction of the Apogee 2300 Digital Color Doppler Ultrasound Imaging System was reported. PROCEPT BioRobotics is an importer of the Apogee 2300 Digital Color Doppler Ultrasound Imaging System. The system is a purchased device hence manufacturer date is not available. The receiving inspection record for the Apogee 2300 Digital Color Doppler Ultrasound Imaging System Serial Number (b)(6)was reviewed. It passed the receiving inspection. No reworks were performed by PROCEPT BioRobotics that were related to the reported event. The review indicated that the device met specifications when released for distribution.The treatment log files were reviewed, which confirmed no malfunction occurred and the system functioned as intended.The review of the Operation Manual for the Apogee 2300 device (IFU) found that it has covered the related safety instruction:1.6 Safety.l) When performing the rectal ultrasound exam, be gentle in the movement. Do not perform violent operation, otherwise it may cause risks of perforation of the rectal wall, damage to the anus and perianal tissues, damage to the rectal mucosa or bleeding.The Apogee 2300 Digital Color Doppler Ultrasound Imaging System is a reusable device; therefore, it is still currently in possession of the user facility. The ECBP-1, SIUI TRUS Probe was not returned for investigation of this complaint. It was reported that post-Aquablation therapy, the patient presented with a rectal perforation. The patient required additional surgery to repair the perforation and was required to have a temporary stoma in place as part of the postoperative management. According to the treating surgeon, the confirmed cause of the perforation remains unknown. Based on review of the information provided, plus a review of the treatment log files, and IFU, the root cause is considered to be undeterminable.Submission of this report does not constitute an admission that the manufacturer's product caused or contributed to the event.

records.reason_for_recall: GE HealthCare has become aware of an issue with certain IC9-RS ultrasound probes (see Affected Products List) that can result in a double image artifact creating a ghost image with realistic features. An unrecognized artifact may lead to misdiagnosis.

records.product_description: bkActiv Ultrasound System 2300, Model numbers 2300-56 and 2300-66.
records.reason_for_recall: An issue on the Dual Live Compare feature on the bkActiv system could result in a measurement error.

records.product_description: Philips EPIQ Diagnostic Ultrasound System Models:  EPIQ 7G(model # 795200), EPIQ 7C (Model # 795201), EPIQ 7W (Model # 795202), EPIQ 5G (model # 795204), EPIQ 5W (model # 795206), EPIQ CVx (Model # 795231), EPIQ Elite (model # 795234)
records.reason_for_recall: Their is the potential that diagnostic ultrasound systems operating with software version 10.0 may present a delayed image instead of a real time image.
